4.say: Check that. Nervous tissue is not about feeling nervous. What does it carry?
hit: Nervous tissue makes you nervous when you are scared.
nervous tissue is what makes people feel anxious
miss: Nervous tissue transmits nerve impulses (messages) throughout the body.
Nervous tissue sends messages through the body, like from your brain to your hand.
It does not make you nervous; it carries nerve impulses.

5.say: Check that. Can you choose when your heart beats? Heart muscle is involuntary.
hit: Muscle tissue makes movement. Your heart is voluntary.
You control your heartbeat with muscle tissue.
you choose when your heart beats
miss: Muscle tissue makes movement possible, both voluntary and involuntary.
Some is voluntary like arm muscles and some is involuntary like the heart.
You cannot control your heartbeat, it is involuntary.
The heart muscle is involuntary and the leg muscles are voluntary.

6.say: Check that. Do internal conditions match the outside, or stay constant when the outside changes?
hit: Homeostasis is when your body temperature matches the outside.
the body changes with the environment
miss: Homeostasis is the relatively constant internal conditions that organisms maintain, even when things change around them.
The inside stays constant and does not match the outside.
Homeostasis keeps the inside steady even when the environment changes.
even when the weather changes the inside stays about the same

7.say: Check that. That is an example of positive feedback. Negative feedback brings conditions back to normal.
hit: Negative feedback example: childbirth contractions get stronger.
an example of negative feedback is blood clotting
miss: Feedback inhibition is when a change causes a response that pushes conditions back toward normal. Example: a thermostat turns the furnace on when the room gets cold.
Childbirth is an example of positive feedback, not negative feedback.
Negative feedback is like a thermostat; positive feedback is like childbirth.
It pushes things back to normal, like shivering when you are cold.

13.say: Check that. An alveolus is a tiny air sac. The blood vessels around it are capillaries.
hit: An alveolus is a blood vessel in the lungs where gas exchange happens.
alveoli are capillaries in the lungs
miss: An alveolus is a tiny air sac in the lungs where gas exchange happens.
Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries.
The alveoli are where oxygen moves into the capillaries.
Alveoli are not blood vessels, they are air sacs.

15.say: Check that. The esophagus carries food. Which tube does air go down?
hit: Air goes through the nose, pharynx, larynx then esophagus.
the air goes down the esophagus to the lungs
miss: Air goes through the nose (nasal cavity), pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and into the alveoli in the lungs.
The pharynx leads to both the trachea and the esophagus, but air goes to the trachea.
Air goes through the nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, and alveoli. Food goes down the esophagus.

15.say: Check that. Is the diaphragm above or below the lungs?
hit: The diaphragm is above the lungs.
the diaphragm sits on top of the lungs
miss: The diaphragm is the muscle under the lungs.
The diaphragm is a muscle below the lungs.
The lungs are above the diaphragm.

16.re: (?<!\b(not|never|don't|dont|doesn't|doesnt|no)\b.{0,10})\b(exhal\w*|breathe out|breathes out|breathed out|breathing out) (the )?(oxygen|o2|o 2)\b|(?<!\b(not|never|don't|dont|doesn't|doesnt|no)\b.{0,10})\b(inhal\w*|breathe in|breathes in|breathing in) (the )?(carbon dioxide|co2|co 2)\b
16.say: Check that. Which gas do you breathe in, and which do you breathe out?
hit: We breathe out oxygen and breathe in carbon dioxide.
carbon dioxide goes into the alveoli and you exhale oxygen
miss: Gas exchange happens between the alveoli and the capillaries. Oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood. Carbon dioxide moves from the blood into the alveoli to be breathed out.
We inhale oxygen and exhale carbon dioxide.
You do not breathe out oxygen, you breathe out carbon dioxide.

17.re: \binhal\w* (the |your )?(chest|lungs?|chest cavity|rib cage) (gets?|becomes?|goes) smaller\b|\bexhal\w* (the |your )?(chest|lungs?|chest cavity|rib cage) (gets?|becomes?) bigger\b
17.say: Check that. When you inhale, does your chest get bigger or smaller?
hit: when you inhale your chest gets smaller
when you exhale the lungs get bigger
miss: When you inhale, the diaphragm contracts and moves down, making the chest bigger and pulling air in. When you exhale, it relaxes and moves up, pushing air out.
When you inhale the chest gets bigger. When you exhale it gets smaller.
Inhale: diaphragm contracts and moves down. Exhale: diaphragm relaxes and moves up.

18.say: Check that. The medulla responds to rising carbon dioxide. Which gas does it sense?
hit: The medulla senses low oxygen and tells the lungs to breathe faster.
the medulla detects oxygen in the blood
miss: When carbon dioxide in the blood rises, sensors in the blood vessels signal the medulla oblongata. The medulla tells the lungs to breathe faster.
When carbon dioxide goes up, the medulla senses it and makes you breathe faster.
The medulla senses carbon dioxide, not oxygen, and speeds up breathing.
